<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.

<!-- Project rules for agents (Claude, pi, codex). CLAUDE.md inlines this into every session — keep this file lean. Put package-specific detail in the nearest package AGENTS.md. -->

## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

Fair challenge — let me give you the exact accounting, because the number matters and so does what it buys. The real figure is **+1,443 / −56** against main. Here's where every line goes:

| chunk | lines | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| tests | +570 | 4 suites pinning the concurrency behavior + mutation coverage |
| staleness *detection* | ~360 | fingerprint resolver (+205), lease expiry + minTtl (+100), PG liveness probe (+55) |
| the gate + wiring | ~250 | `dispatch-recycle.ts` (187, of which ~half is comments) + job-router/gateway wiring |
| bookkeeping in deployment-manager | ~200 | record fingerprint/expiry at create, recycle impl, revocation backstop |
| payload stamp | ~55 | one field on `MessagePayload` + consumer stamping |

The justification, plainly: **this isn't reliability polish on working code — it's the fix for a live, security-relevant bug.** Today in prod, a warm worker outlives its credential (gh starts 401ing after ~1h), keeps acting as a *repointed* installation's old identity, and keeps executing with *revoked* credentials. You can't fix that in zero lines: ~360 of these lines exist because you cannot detect "stale" without computing what "current" is, and ~570 are tests — which is exactly the line item your bug history says never to skimp on for concurrency code. The alternative on the table was never "no lines"; it was #2234's +3,318 or the bug staying in prod.

That said, two parts of your complaint are correct and I'll act on both:

1. **The comment weight is real.** `dispatch-recycle.ts` makes the fail-closed argument three separate times; the module could lose 100–200 lines of prose without losing any constraint. The fixer pass you just backgrounded is editing the tree right now; the moment it finishes I'll do a trim pass on comment redundancy before pushing — cutting explanation, never checks.
2. **"Hard to follow" is on me.** Crisp state: **merged** — #2312, the two AGENTS.md invariants (+2 net lines). **Pending** — this one PR, the recycle fix. **Planned after it** — nothing. Merge, close #2234 (which *removes* a 3,300-line liability from the review queue), delete the worktrees, prod-verify. No phase 2, no lease-refresh, no further code unless prod data demands it. This PR is the last addition of the program.

If after seeing the trimmed diff you still think the cost is wrong, the honest fallback isn't a smaller version of this fix — it's shipping only the revocation/fingerprint half and accepting hourly credential death on active conversations, which I don't recommend. I'll show you the final numbers when the fixer completes and I've done the trim.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

<!-- Project rules for agents (Claude, pi, codex). CLAUDE.md inlines this into every session — keep this file lean. Put package-specific detail in the nearest package AGENTS.md. -->

## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

288-	@./scripts/review-fix.sh $(if $(BASE),--base $(BASE),)

290-# Fast, deterministic CI gates that need NO database — the exact checks that
291-# `make review` (LLM-verdict only) does NOT run. Run this before opening/updating

294-# touch server/runtime code — but it catches the cheap, common misses.

299-	@# field the dist predates) — the exact trap CI avoids by building first.

302-	@bun run typecheck

287:review-fix:
288-	@./scripts/review-fix.sh $(if $(BASE),--base $(BASE),)
289-
290-# Fast, deterministic CI gates that need NO database — the exact checks that
291-# `make review` (LLM-verdict only) does NOT run. Run this before opening/updating
292-# a PR so knip / typecheck / lint failures don't surface only in CI.
293-# NOT a substitute for the DB-backed suites (make test-integration) when you
294-# touch server/runtime code — but it catches the cheap, common misses.
295-pre-pr:
296-	@echo "🔎 [1/6] Build workspace packages (fresh dist)..."
297-	@# Typecheck resolves @lobu/* against built dist, not src. Without this a
298-	@# stale core dist yields PHANTOM errors on any contract change (e.g. a new
299-	@# field the dist predates) — the exact trap CI avoids by building first.
300-	@make build-packages
301-	@echo "🔎 [2/6] Strict typecheck (root + excluded packages)..."
302-	@bun run typecheck

**The line-count question is settled, with the trim landed and re-verified.** The branch now stands at **+2,016 gross / −124 (net ~+1,890) across 19 files**, and that number was already after a −335-line simplification pass that I reviewed hunk-by-hunk and adopted:

- The **reconcile revocation backstop is gone** (~250 lines src+test). Its marginal value was small: worker credentials are short-lived leases that die by TTL, and no turn can execute without passing the dispatch gate — the backstop only reaped an idle sandbox holding a token that was about to expire anyway. It was exactly the "second mechanism" our new AGENTS.md brake warns against.
- **Tooling resolution now fails hard** instead of degrading to "no contribution," which deleted the `UNKNOWN_TOOLING_FINGERPRINT` sentinel machinery and all its special-casing. I verified the resolver still degrades gracefully on malformed declarations internally, so only genuine infrastructure errors propagate — consistent with the fail-closed invariant.

Of the ~1,890 net lines, **~1,088 (57%) are tests** — and those tests are not padding: I re-ran all four mutations against the trimmed code and each one bites (gate disabled → 5 failures; liveness probe neutralized → 1; fail-open error path → 1; lease TTL floor removed → 1). All 126 tests green on the real code.

One incident worth reporting: the earlier review-fix run raced my mutation testing and its single edit turned out to be "fixing" my own deliberately-broken line; my restore wiped it and HEAD was already correct. Because that run's verdict was contaminated, I've restarted `make review-fix` on the settled, committed tree. input.content:
## Summary
- Replaces the enqueue-side recycle approach of #2234: a warm worker deployment currently outlives its connector credentials — a GitHub App lease dies after ~1h, and a repointed/revoked installation keeps acting under the old identity until the idle reaper runs.
- Recycles at the **dispatch chokepoint** instead of at enqueue. Dispatch is already single-pod (a worker's queue is registered only by the pod it SSE-connects to, and `handleJob` delivers only via that pod's local connection registry), so staleness is checked exactly where no cross-replica coordination exists — no advisory locks, no hold/requeue machinery, no new tables. Queue-native retry (handler throw) is the only deferral mechanism, and every error path fails closed: an error never delivers a turn to a stale worker.
- Mechanics: the enqueue path stamps a `toolingFingerprint` (SHA-256 of connection identity — never credential material) onto the job payload; the owner pod compares it against what the deployment was built with, plus a pod-local lease-expiry check with a 10-minute floor so the cache never re-serves a dying token. Stale + quiet → tear down and rebuild under the same name; stale + a prior turn live → defer via queue retry. The liveness probe excludes armed-but-undelivered turns so two queued turns can't defer each other forever.
- Tooling resolution now **fails hard** on infrastructure errors (the fingerprint is durable dispatch state; a failed DB lookup must not read as "no evidence of change"), while malformed declarations still degrade gracefully inside the resolver. The earlier reconcile-loop revocation backstop was deliberately dropped: leases die by TTL and no turn executes without passing this gate, so it was a second mechanism guarding the same invariant.
- Review-fix caught (and this PR includes) a real cache bug: the GitHub installation-token cache key ignored the resolved App identity, so repointing an installation at a different App would serve the old App's cached token to the freshly recycled worker — defeating the recycle. The key now includes the resolved `appId`.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: targeted `bun test` on all 7 touched suites — 127 pass, 0 fail (includes the DB-backed resolver, enqueue, and liveness-probe suites; run locally against Postgres — the review-fix sandbox could not bind loopback ports, so its DB-suite pass is mine, not the fixer's)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] Full `make test-integration` sweep not run in this session; CI's integration job is the authoritative pass

### Red→green evidence
Red (dispatch gate disabled — mutation `if (this.dispatchRecycler)` → `if (false)` in `job-router.ts`):
```
 5 fail
 59 expect() calls
Ran 33 tests across 2 files.
```
Green (gate active, same suites):
```
 33 pass / 0 fail across worker-dispatch-recycle + worker-job-router
 127 pass / 0 fail across all touched suites
```

### Mutation evidence (each mutation applied to src, suite run, then reverted)
| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Disable the dispatch gate (`if (false)`) | 5 tests fail |
| M2 | Neutralize the live-turn probe (`if (false)`) | 1 test fails (mid-turn SIGTERM protection) |
| M3 | Fail open on recycle error (`throw` → `return`) | 1 test fails (fail-closed contract) |
| M4 | `LEASE_MIN_TTL_MS` 10min → 0 | 1 test fails (dying-token cache floor) |
| M5 | Drop resolved `appId` from token cache key | 1 test fails (App-repoint cache poisoning) |

## Notes
- Supersedes #2234 (enqueue-side recycle; advisory-lock/hold-requeue approach). Closing it in favor of this PR.
- Net diff is +2,065/−129 across 19 files, of which ~57% is tests; there are no new tables, no deployment-name changes, and no new coordination primitives.
- Follow-up deliberately NOT planned: mid-turn lease refresh stays out of scope unless prod shows recycle churn or mid-turn 401s (tracked via post-rollout verification).

* True when ANY turn is still in flight on `deploymentName`.
 *
 * Deployment-scoped sibling of {@link hasLiveTurnForMessage}, for callers that
 * are about to tear a worker down and must not interrupt a turn already
 * running on it — recycling a deployment for a stale credential must never
 * SIGTERM a live run and cost the user a reply.
 *
 * Postgres-backed rather than pod-local, so it is correct with N replicas: the
 * turn may have been started by a different pod than the one deciding to
 * recycle.
 *
 * Same index probe and same `run_at > now()` deadline predicate as
 * {@link hasLiveTurnForMessage} — a lapsed-but-unswept marker is a dead worker,
 * not a live turn, and must not block a recycle forever.
 *
 * "In flight" here means a turn the worker has actually RECEIVED. A turn's
 * marker is armed at dispatch, BEFORE its
 * `thread_message_*` job is delivered, so an armed-but-still-queued turn has a
 * live marker while its job sits `pending`/`claimed` on the worker queue. The
 * recycle gate ignores those: it runs while holding one such claimed job, and
 * two queued turns would otherwise each read the other's marker as "a running
 * turn" and defer each other forever. A marker whose `thread_message` job row
 * is gone (completed on delivery receipt) is a turn that reached the worker —
 * exactly the turns a teardown would interrupt.
 */
export async function hasLiveTurnForDeployment(
  deploymentName: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  const sql = getDb();
  const rows = await sql<{ ok: number }>`
    SELECT 1 AS ok FROM public.runs m
    WHERE m.status = 'pending'
      AND m.run_type = 'internal'
      AND m.queue_name = ${TURN_TIMEOUT_QUEUE}
      AND m.action_input->>'deploymentName' = ${deploymentName}
      AND m.run_at > now()
      AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM public.runs q
        WHERE q.status IN ('pending', 'claimed')
          AND q.run_type = 'chat_message'
          AND q.queue_name = ${`thread_message_${deploymentName}`}
          AND q.action_input->>'messageId' = m.action_input->>'messageId'
      )
    LIMIT 1
  `;
  return rows.length > 0;
}

1	/**
2	 * Turn liveness — surfaces a terminal error to the client when a worker fails
3	 * to produce a reply (crash, hang, or pod death), so the SSE/CLI never hangs
4	 * forever and never receives a silent `complete`.
5	 *
6	 * ## The obligation, as a durable election record
7	 *
8	 * Every dispatched turn owes the client exactly one terminal event for its
9	 * `messageId`. Between delivery-receipt (when the `thread_message` run already
10	 * completes) and the worker's reply there is otherwise NO durable record that
11	 * the turn is still owed an answer — that gap is what lets a dead worker hang
12	 * the stream. We close it by writing a **passive marker row** into `public.runs`
13	 * on a queue with NO consumer (`internal:turn_timeout`): it is never claimed as
14	 * a job, so the RunsQueue status machinery never touches it. The marker's
15	 * EXISTENCE is the obligation; deleting it (`DELETE … RETURNING`) is a
16	 * first-writer-wins election — a row can be deleted exactly once, and the
17	 * deleter emits the terminal `error` in the SAME transaction, so the emit is
18	 * atomic and crash-safe (the marker survives a mid-emit crash and a later sweep
19	 * retries).
20	 *
21	 * ## Detection (two paths, one emit)
22	 *  - Fast path (instant): the owning pod observes `child.once("exit"/"error")`
23	 *    and calls {@link failTurnsForDeployment}. Covers the common case (bad
24	 *    provider key, OOM, `exit 1`).
25	 *  - Backstop (deadline): {@link sweepExpiredTurns} runs periodically on every
26	 *    replica and fails markers whose deadline has lapsed. Covers a hung worker
27	 *    (alive, never replies) and a worker-pod death (the marker outlives the pod
28	 *    and another replica sweeps it). The deadline is pushed forward
29	 *    ({@link extendTurnDeadlines}) by any worker-driven liveness signal —
30	 *    primarily the worker's 20s status_update, plus the 30s SSE-ping ACK and
31	 *    delivery receipts — so a live-but-slow worker is never falsely failed,
32	 *    while a silent one lapses.
33	 *
34	 * ## Multi-replica
35	 * Arming/extending/discharging all happen on the worker's owning pod (worker
36	 * child, dispatch, and `handleWorkerResponse` are co-located there). The marker
37	 * + emit live in shared Postgres, so any replica can sweep, and the emitted
38	 * `thread_response{error}` is owner-gated in `routeToRenderer` to reach the pod
39	 * that holds the client's SSE.
40	 */

## Summary
- Replaces the enqueue-side recycle approach of #2234: a warm worker deployment currently outlives its connector credentials — a GitHub App lease dies after ~1h, and a repointed/revoked installation keeps acting under the old identity until the idle reaper runs.
- Recycles at the **dispatch chokepoint** instead of at enqueue. Dispatch is already single-pod (a worker's queue is registered only by the pod it SSE-connects to, and `handleJob` delivers only via that pod's local connection registry), so staleness is checked exactly where no cross-replica coordination exists — no advisory locks, no hold/requeue machinery, no new tables. Queue-native retry (handler throw) is the only deferral mechanism, and every error path fails closed: an error never delivers a turn to a stale worker.
- Mechanics: the enqueue path stamps a `toolingFingerprint` (SHA-256 of connection identity — never credential material) onto the job payload; the owner pod compares it against what the deployment was built with, plus a pod-local lease-expiry check with a 10-minute floor so the cache never re-serves a dying token. Stale + quiet → tear down and rebuild under the same name; stale + a prior turn live → defer via queue retry. The liveness probe excludes armed-but-undelivered turns so two queued turns can't defer each other forever.
- Tooling resolution now **fails hard** on infrastructure errors (the fingerprint is durable dispatch state; a failed DB lookup must not read as "no evidence of change"), while malformed declarations still degrade gracefully inside the resolver. The earlier reconcile-loop revocation backstop was deliberately dropped: leases die by TTL and no turn executes without passing this gate, so it was a second mechanism guarding the same invariant.
- Review-fix caught (and this PR includes) a real cache bug: the GitHub installation-token cache key ignored the resolved App identity, so repointing an installation at a different App would serve the old App's cached token to the freshly recycled worker — defeating the recycle. The key now includes the resolved `appId`.

The review round-1 blocker is fixed, pushed, and review round 2 is running against the corrected HEAD — a second round is the sanctioned path when round 1 finds a genuine blocker (as opposed to iterating review as a find-fix loop).

What just happened, briefly: the reviewer caught a real race I'd missed. The liveness probe treated "a pending job row exists for this messageId" as proof the turn was never delivered — but when a worker's SSE connection drops and reconnects mid-turn, `registerWorker` replays the still-running turn's durable input onto the queue, creating exactly such a pending row. The probe would then have called the running turn "not live" and allowed a recycle to SIGTERM an active worker. The fix inverts the evidence: a turn counts as live only on its positive delivery receipt (a completed `thread_message` row, retained 30 days), which is simpler than the old exclusion and immune to replay rows. Proven red→green (2 regression tests fail under the old semantics, 129/129 pass with the fix) and committed as `603bc171c`.

When the review verdict and CI land: merge on green, close #2234, cleanup, prod-verify wakeup.

lines: +  // The replay exists to restore turns whose QUEUE ROW is gone (expired-pending
+  // cleanup deletes jobs a disconnected worker never claimed). A row in ANY
+  // state means the queue still owns the turn: pending/claimed is the original
+  // job awaiting delivery or a dispatch-gate deferral retry, completed is a
+  // delivered turn the (reconnecting) worker is already running. Re-sending
+  // over such a row delivers the same turn twice — the recycle path holds its
+  // claimed job across the rebuild, so without this predicate every recycle
+  // would double-deliver the very turn that triggered it.

## Summary
- Replaces the enqueue-side recycle approach of #2234: a warm worker deployment currently outlives its connector credentials — a GitHub App lease dies after ~1h, and a repointed/revoked installation keeps acting under the old identity until the idle reaper runs.
- Recycles at the **dispatch chokepoint** instead of at enqueue. Dispatch is already single-pod (a worker's queue is registered only by the pod it SSE-connects to, and `handleJob` delivers only via that pod's local connection registry), so staleness is checked exactly where no cross-replica coordination exists — no advisory locks, no hold/requeue machinery, no new tables. Queue-native retry (handler throw) is the only deferral mechanism, and every error path fails closed: an error never delivers a turn to a stale worker.
- Mechanics: the enqueue path stamps a `toolingFingerprint` (SHA-256 of connection identity — never credential material) onto the job payload; the owner pod compares it against what the deployment was built with, plus a pod-local lease-expiry check with a 10-minute floor so the cache never re-serves a dying token. Stale + quiet → tear down and rebuild under the same name; stale + a prior turn live → defer via queue retry. The liveness probe excludes armed-but-undelivered turns so two queued turns can't defer each other forever.
- Tooling resolution now **fails hard** on infrastructure errors (the fingerprint is durable dispatch state; a failed DB lookup must not read as "no evidence of change"), while malformed declarations still degrade gracefully inside the resolver. The earlier reconcile-loop revocation backstop was deliberately dropped: leases die by TTL and no turn executes without passing this gate, so it was a second mechanism guarding the same invariant.
- Review-fix caught (and this PR includes) a real cache bug: the GitHub installation-token cache key ignored the resolved App identity, so repointing an installation at a different App would serve the old App's cached token to the freshly recycled worker — defeating the recycle. The key now includes the resolved `appId`.
- The first `make review` round found a genuine blocker in the liveness probe, fixed in the second commit: the probe read "no pending/claimed job row" as delivery evidence, but an SSE reconnect replays the durable input of a still-**running** turn (`registerWorker`), creating a fresh pending row for the same messageId — which made the running turn look undelivered and would have let a recycle SIGTERM an active worker. The probe now consults the positive delivery receipt instead (a **completed** `thread_message` row, retained 30 days), which is both simpler and correct for replay rows.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: targeted `bun test` on all 7 touched suites — 127 pass, 0 fail (includes the DB-backed resolver, enqueue, and liveness-probe suites; run locally against Postgres — the review-fix sandbox could not bind loopback ports, so its DB-suite pass is mine, not the fixer's)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] Full `make test-integration` sweep not run in this session; CI's integration job is the authoritative pass

axes.** `bug_free_confidence`, `slop`, and `simplicity` are
> independent. A change can score high `bug_free_confidence` (works), high
> `slop` (lots of unused code added), and low `simplicity` (overengineered).
> The `pi-review` status requires all seven gates to pass: these three metrics,
> `bugs == 0`, `blockers.length == 0`, `behavior_change_risk != "high"`, and
> `tests_adequate == true`.

### `blockers` (array of strings)

One-line descriptions of issues **caused by this diff** that should block
merge regardless of the other scores. Empty array if none. Examples:

- `"introduces a secret in a committed file"`
- `"db migration is not idempotent"`
- `"deletes a public export still used by @lobu/cli"`

Pre-existing environmental failures (test suite broken on `main`, missing
workspace export from an unrelated package, Postgres schema-ACL issue in
test setup) are NOT blockers — they belong in `notes` with an `[env]`
prefix. A failing test only blocks when the failing test, or the source
code it exercises, appears in `git diff --name-only "$BASE_BRANCH...HEAD"`.

**Gate:** `make review` passes only when `blockers.length == 0`.

### `change_type` (enum)

One of: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `deps`.

Maps to conventional-commit prefix. Use the prefix that best describes the
**primary** intent of the diff. If the PR genuinely does two things in equal
measure (e.g. `feat` + `test`), prefer `feat`. If you would split this PR,
say so in `notes`.

**Note:** the current `pi-review` status applies one gate policy to all change
types. If a docs/chore/test PR needs an exception, use an explicit env override
or admin merge.

### `behavior_change_risk` (enum)

One of: `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`.

- **none** — pure refactor, docs, type-only changes. No runtime behavior
  reaches users.
- **low** — behavior change is bounded to a narrow code path with adequate
  tests, or to a dev-only / opt-in surface.
- **medium** — behavior change affects a path users hit but is well-typed and
  tested, or affects an internal API with multiple call sites.
- **high** — behavior change touches a hot path, migrations, auth, billing,
  data integrity, or anything with cross-system consequences (queue,
  scheduler, retry).

**Gate:** `make review` fails when risk is `high`; that path requires human
approval / admin merge even if scores otherwise pass.

### `tests_adequate` (boolean)

`true` if the diff includes tests covering the behavior change (or no tests
are warranted because behavior_change_risk is `none`). `false` if a
behavior change ships without test coverage.

**Gate:** `make review` fails when `tests_adequate` is `false`. For docs/chore
exceptions, use an explicit env override or admin merge.

### `suggested_fixes` (array of objects)

Specific actionable suggestions. Each object has `file`, `line`, `change`.
Empty array if none.

These are read by the local coding agent and applied between review
iterations — not by the reviewer itself. Be specific (file path + line +
concrete change). Vibe suggestions ("consider refactoring", "this could be cleaner")
don't belong here — the agent can't act on them; surface those as `notes`
instead.

### `notes` (string)

A freeform paragraph (one paragraph, not a wall of text) summarizing the
reviewer's overall take. This is what shows up in the PR comment above
the JSON. Keep it under ~500 chars.

### `categories` (object)

Line counts by category. Sum should approximate `additions + deletions`.

## Summary
- Replaces the enqueue-side recycle approach of #2234: a warm worker deployment currently outlives its connector credentials — a GitHub App lease dies after ~1h, and a repointed/revoked installation keeps acting under the old identity until the idle reaper runs.
- Recycles at the **dispatch chokepoint** instead of at enqueue. Dispatch is already single-pod (a worker's queue is registered only by the pod it SSE-connects to, and `handleJob` delivers only via that pod's local connection registry), so staleness is checked exactly where no cross-replica coordination exists — no advisory locks, no hold/requeue machinery, no new tables. Queue-native retry (handler throw) is the only deferral mechanism, and every error path fails closed: an error never delivers a turn to a stale worker.
- Mechanics: the enqueue path stamps a `toolingFingerprint` (SHA-256 of connection identity — never credential material) onto the job payload; the owner pod compares it against what the deployment was built with, plus a pod-local lease-expiry check with a 10-minute floor so the cache never re-serves a dying token. content.text:
Fair ask. Let me lay out each decision that survived, what the alternative was, and whether I'd make the same call again with a cold head.

**1. Liveness probe: positive delivery receipt instead of "no pending row".** The original inferred "delivered" from the *absence* of queued rows; the fix requires the *presence* of a completed row. Absence-of-evidence broke the moment the replay path created rows the original author didn't anticipate — positive evidence can't break that way. This is strictly better, not churn. Its one fragility: it leans on ack-on-delivery semantics staying true; if someone ever changes the queue to ack-on-turn-end, the probe silently degrades. That invariant is now documented at both ends and pinned by DB tests, which is the best available defense short of the consolidation program.

**2. Replay suppression: skip any turn the queue still owns.** The alternative was the reviewer's singletonKey — I stand by rejecting it, because our own P0 memory says the singleton machinery blocks on expired rows, which converts "duplicate turn" into "silently dropped turn," a strictly worse failure. But I owe you the one real trade-off in this decision: when a *pod dies mid-turn* on a remote runtime, the old replay could sometimes salvage that turn by re-executing it; the new predicate errors it at the sweep deadline instead. The signal is genuinely ambiguous — "worker died holding the turn" and "worker is running the turn right now" look identical in the data — so you must pick a failure mode. I picked honest-error over possible-duplicate-side-effects. I think that's right, and it's the kind of ambiguity only the single-lifecycle-record redesign can actually remove.

**3. Rebuild-failure: terminalize + consume the job.** Alternative was re-throw (silent hang until sweep, then a zombie) or the general dead-turn probe I built and then cut. The landed version reuses the exact election the enqueue path already uses for create failures — it makes recycle-failure behave *identically* to create-failure, which is a consistency win, not an addition. Cutting the general probe was correct: it taxed every delivery with a DB query to close a pre-existing, election-bounded race that isn't this PR's to fix.

**4. The trim (backstop deletion, fail-hard resolution).** Still the right call — the backstop was a second mechanism guarding an invariant the gate already guards, and leases die by TTL regardless.

On the churn itself, honestly: two of the reverts were my own process mistakes (`git checkout` wiping uncommitted fixes, twice — both recovered, both now committed-before-mutating), and one was me over-building until you pushed back. The *path* was noisy; the **final diff is coherent** — every surviving change either fixes a two-store disagreement with the narrowest patch that reuses an existing primitive, or deletes a redundant mechanism. Nothing in the final state contradicts anything else in it.

The only alternative I'd flag as genuinely arguable: don't merge, and jump straight to the turn-lifecycle consolidation. I considered it and I'd vote no — that's a multi-week program, prod keeps serving dying credentials meanwhile, and the consolidation will want exactly these tests as its safety net. Merge this, stop, design that properly.

Round-6 review is still running; I'll act on its result when it posts.

content.text: Good — let's design this properly. I've mapped the solution space; before I write the design, four decisions are genuinely yours. Context for each is in the option descriptions, and my recommendation is marked.

questions.question: What happens to PR #2315 (the claim-side recycle, currently in review round 6) while we build the long-term fix?

options.label: Merge #2315 first (Recommended)
options.description: Prod stops serving dying/revoked credentials now, and its ~1,100 test lines become the safety net the consolidation refactors against. The consolidation then supersedes its patch-layer internally without changing behavior.

options.label: Hold #2315, consolidate first
options.description: No interim patch layer ever lands, but prod keeps the credential bug for the weeks the consolidation takes, and we refactor without the test net on the exact seams we're changing.

questions.question: What becomes the single source of truth for a turn's lifecycle (queued → delivered → answered/failed)?

options.label: Evolve agent_run_input (Recommended)
options.description: It already has the right key (org, deployment, messageId), the payload, and a status column. Add status machine (queued/delivered/answered/failed), deadline_at, delivered_at; terminal transitions become the election (UPDATE...WHERE status not terminal). The liveness-marker rows die entirely. Optionally rename the table to `turn`. No new table, one migration.

options.label: New clean `turn` table
options.description: Fresh schema designed for purpose, agent_run_input migrated into it then dropped. Cleaner end state, but a data migration plus a transition window where both exist — more moving parts for the same authority.

options.label: Queue row as authority
options.description: Extend the runs job row to carry turn status past 'completed'. Cheapest on paper but fights the queue's own semantics (retention, cleanup, ack, retry all assume job rows are ephemeral work items) — I'd advise against.

questions.question: Does the thread_message queue survive as the delivery transport, or do we dispatch straight from turn records?

options.label: Keep queue as transport (Recommended)
options.description: RunsQueue keeps doing claim/retry/backoff/pause — machinery that's battle-tested — but job rows lose ALL lifecycle meaning: the turn record alone says delivered/answered. The replay ambiguity dies because 'queued vs delivered' is read from the turn row, never inferred from job rows.

options.label: Dispatch from turn records directly
options.description: The owner pod delivers turns straight off the turn table (NOTIFY + claim on turn rows); the per-deployment thread_message queues disappear entirely — one less store, the deepest simplification. Cost: reimplementing claim/retry/backoff/pause semantics we currently get for free, which is where new bugs would live.

questions.question: Deployment tooling state (fingerprint, lease expiry) — stay pod-local or persist per deployment?

This is the table you vetoed for v2 — there it was avoidable; for the long-term design it's what makes recycle correct across pod restarts.

options.label: Keep pod-local maps
options.description: Zero new storage; embedded workers die with their pod so the maps are usually right. Accepts permanently that a remote worker adopted by a new pod dodges the staleness gate until idle-reap.

## Summary
- Replaces the enqueue-side recycle approach of #2234: a warm worker deployment currently outlives its connector credentials — a GitHub App lease dies after ~1h, and a repointed/revoked installation keeps acting under the old identity until the idle reaper runs.
- Recycles at the **dispatch chokepoint** instead of at enqueue. Dispatch is already single-pod (a worker's queue is registered only by the pod it SSE-connects to, and `handleJob` delivers only via that pod's local connection registry), so staleness is checked exactly where no cross-replica coordination exists — no advisory locks, no hold/requeue machinery, no new tables. Queue-native retry (handler throw) is the only deferral mechanism, and every error path fails closed: an error never delivers a turn to a stale worker.
- Mechanics: the enqueue path stamps a `toolingFingerprint` (SHA-256 of connection identity — never credential material) onto the job payload; the owner pod compares it against what the deployment was built with, plus a pod-local lease-expiry check with a 10-minute floor so the cache never re-serves a dying token. Stale + quiet → tear down and rebuild under the same name; stale + a prior turn live → defer via queue retry. The liveness probe excludes armed-but-undelivered turns so two queued turns can't defer each other forever.
- Tooling resolution now **fails hard** on infrastructure errors (the fingerprint is durable dispatch state; a failed DB lookup must not read as "no evidence of change"), while malformed declarations still degrade gracefully inside the resolver. The earlier reconcile-loop revocation backstop was deliberately dropped: leases die by TTL and no turn executes without passing this gate, so it was a second mechanism guarding the same invariant.
- Review-fix caught (and this PR includes) a real cache bug: the GitHub installation-token cache key ignored the resolved App identity, so repointing an installation at a different App would serve the old App's cached token to the freshly recycled worker — defeating the recycle. The key now includes the resolved `appId`.
- Review round 5 found a stranded-turn blocker, fixed in the fifth commit: if the recycle's *rebuild* step fails after the teardown, the SSE disconnect has paused the queue's only consumer, so the re-thrown job sat unclaimable until the sweep deadline and could later be delivered as a zombie once a new message rebuilt the worker. The gate now terminalizes the held turn through the same marker election the enqueue path uses for create failures (`failTurnIfPending(WORKER_STARTUP_FAILED)`) and completes the job it is holding — prompt user-visible error, no pending job, no zombie. If the terminalize itself fails, the original error still propagates (fail closed; sweep remains the backstop).
- Review round 3 found a duplicate-delivery blocker, fixed in the fourth commit: the recycle rebuilds the worker while the gate still holds the claimed job, and the fresh worker's `registerWorker` replay re-enqueued the same turn's durable input as a second job — both then deliver. Fixed at the replay source: `listPendingAgentRunInputs` now skips any input whose turn still has a queue row in ANY state (pending = awaiting deferral retry, claimed = held across the recycle, completed = the reconnecting worker is already running it) — the replay exists solely to restore rows the expired-pending cleanup deleted. The reviewer's singletonKey suggestion was deliberately not taken: the singleton machinery has a known unfixed bug where it blocks on expired rows, which would trade a duplicate turn for a silently dropped one.
- The first `make review` round found a genuine blocker in the liveness probe, fixed in the second commit: the probe read "no pending/claimed job row" as delivery evidence, but an SSE reconnect replays the durable input of a still-**running** turn (`registerWorker`), creating a fresh pending row for the same messageId — which made the running turn look undelivered and would have let a recycle SIGTERM an active worker. The probe now consults the positive delivery receipt instead (a **completed** `thread_message` row, retained 30 days), which is both simpler and correct for replay rows.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: targeted `bun test` on all 7 touched suites — 127 pass, 0 fail (includes the DB-backed resolver, enqueue, and liveness-probe suites; run locally against Postgres — the review-fix sandbox could not bind loopback ports, so its DB-suite pass is mine, not the fixer's)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] Full `make test-integration` sweep not run in this session; CI's integration job is the authoritative pass

---
name: deployment-recycle-redesign
description: "Claim-side recycle SHIPPED as PR #2315 (5 review rounds, each blocker = two turn-state stores disagreeing); #2234 closed superseded; NEXT DESIGN DEBT = single turn-lifecycle authority"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 824ebede-b743-4669-bf41-b7dc06ec91c8
  modified: 2026-07-29T16:23:45.571Z
---

**PR #2315** (`feat/claim-side-recycle`) implements the DECIDED v2 claim-side recycle: staleness (tooling fingerprint stamped on payload at enqueue + owner-pod lease-expiry map with 10-min floor) is checked in `gateDispatchOnStaleness` at the dispatch chokepoint (`job-router.handleJob`, single-pod by construction), queue-native throw = the only deferral, fail closed throughout. NO new tables, NO name changes, no advisory locks. Supersedes #2234 (closed) whose enqueue-side design needed the lock/hold machinery — 4 confirmed defects recorded in git history of this file.

**The 5-review-round pattern (why the PR grew to ~2.1k net):** every real blocker was two turn-state stores disagreeing:
1. Probe read "pending job row absent" as delivery evidence → SSE-reconnect replay rows masqueraded as undelivered → fix: positive delivery receipt (completed `thread_message` row) is the only liveness evidence.
2. `registerWorker` replay re-enqueued a turn whose original job was still claimed across the recycle → duplicate delivery → fix: `listPendingAgentRunInputs` skips inputs with ANY surviving queue row (replay exists only for expired-deleted rows). Rejected reviewer's singletonKey fix — singleton machinery has unfixed P0 (blocks on EXPIRED rows) = silent turn drop.
3. Recycle rebuild-failure stranded the held job on a paused queue (SSE teardown pauses the consumer) → hang till sweep + later zombie delivery → fix: terminalize via `failTurnIfPending(WORKER_STARTUP_FAILED)` (same election as enqueue-path create failures) and complete the held job (gate returns "drop").
Also fixed en route: GitHub installation-token cache key ignored resolved App identity (App-repoint served old App's token to the recycled worker); org-less payload = known-empty tooling, not an error (codex pushed that fix to the branch itself — codex pushes to open PR branches under the user's identity).

**TURN-LIFECYCLE CONSOLIDATION — DECIDED 2026-07-29 (user interviewed, 4 decisions):** the follow-up program replacing the 5-store duct tape.
1. **Sequencing**: merge #2315 FIRST (its ~1.1k test lines are the refactor's safety net), then consolidate.
2. **Authority**: evolve `agent_run_input` into THE turn record — add status machine (queued/delivered/answered/failed) + deadline_at + delivered_at; terminal transitions = the election (UPDATE…WHERE status not terminal RETURNING). DELETE the entire marker mechanism (arming, marker election, marker sweep, `internal:turn_timeout` rows) + the replay-suppression predicate + the delivery-receipt probe — all become reads of one row. Must be net-negative mechanisms/lines.
3. **Queue lane**: RunsQueue `thread_message_*` stays as delivery TRANSPORT ONLY; job rows carry zero lifecycle meaning.
4. **Remote-worker pod-restart gap** (remote sandbox — Vercel-style — outlives pod, adopting pod has no fingerprint/lease memory → stale looks fresh): DEFERRED until remote runtimes carry prod traffic. Revisit options then: treat-unknown-as-stale (zero storage, one recycle per deploy) vs per-deployment PG record.

**No lease-refresh phase 2** unless prod shows recycle churn or mid-turn 401s (user-agreed stop).

Related: [[agent-config-composition-roadmap]] (the feature this protects, #2243 merged).

## Summary
- Replaces the enqueue-side recycle approach of #2234: a warm worker deployment currently outlives its connector credentials — a GitHub App lease dies after ~1h, and a repointed/revoked installation keeps acting under the old identity until the idle reaper runs.
- Recycles at the **dispatch chokepoint** instead of at enqueue. Dispatch is already single-pod (a worker's queue is registered only by the pod it SSE-connects to, and `handleJob` delivers only via that pod's local connection registry), so staleness is checked exactly where no cross-replica coordination exists — no advisory locks, no hold/requeue machinery, no new tables. Queue-native retry (handler throw) is the only deferral mechanism, and every error path fails closed: an error never delivers a turn to a stale worker.
- Mechanics: the enqueue path stamps a `toolingFingerprint` (SHA-256 of connection identity — never credential material) onto the job payload; the owner pod compares it against what the deployment was built with, plus a pod-local lease-expiry check with a 10-minute floor so the cache never re-serves a dying token. Stale + quiet → tear down and rebuild under the same name; stale + a prior turn live → defer via queue retry. The liveness probe excludes armed-but-undelivered turns so two queued turns can't defer each other forever.
- Tooling resolution now **fails hard** on infrastructure errors (the fingerprint is durable dispatch state; a failed DB lookup must not read as "no evidence of change"), while malformed declarations still degrade gracefully inside the resolver. The earlier reconcile-loop revocation backstop was deliberately dropped: leases die by TTL and no turn executes without passing this gate, so it was a second mechanism guarding the same invariant.
- Review-fix caught (and this PR includes) a real cache bug: the GitHub installation-token cache key ignored the resolved App identity, so repointing an installation at a different App would serve the old App's cached token to the freshly recycled worker — defeating the recycle. The key now includes the resolved `appId`.
- Review round 6 found that the round-5 fix rested on a swallowed error: `failTurnIfPending` caught its own DB failures and returned `false`, making "election lost (safe to drop)" indistinguishable from "terminalize never happened (dropping loses the turn)". Fixed in the sixth commit by removing the internal catch — infrastructure failures now propagate, and each caller keeps its own policy (`trackFailedDeployment` already had a best-effort catch at its call site; the gate re-throws so the job keeps retrying).
- Review round 5 found a stranded-turn blocker, fixed in the fifth commit: if the recycle's *rebuild* step fails after the teardown, the SSE disconnect has paused the queue's only consumer, so the re-thrown job sat unclaimable until the sweep deadline and could later be delivered as a zombie once a new message rebuilt the worker. The gate now terminalizes the held turn through the same marker election the enqueue path uses for create failures (`failTurnIfPending(WORKER_STARTUP_FAILED)`) and completes the job it is holding — prompt user-visible error, no pending job, no zombie. If the terminalize itself fails, the original error still propagates (fail closed; sweep remains the backstop).
- Review round 3 found a duplicate-delivery blocker, fixed in the fourth commit: the recycle rebuilds the worker while the gate still holds the claimed job, and the fresh worker's `registerWorker` replay re-enqueued the same turn's durable input as a second job — both then deliver. Fixed at the replay source: `listPendingAgentRunInputs` now skips any input whose turn still has a queue row in ANY state (pending = awaiting deferral retry, claimed = held across the recycle, completed = the reconnecting worker is already running it) — the replay exists solely to restore rows the expired-pending cleanup deleted. The reviewer's singletonKey suggestion was deliberately not taken: the singleton machinery has a known unfixed bug where it blocks on expired rows, which would trade a duplicate turn for a silently dropped one.
- The first `make review` round found a genuine blocker in the liveness probe, fixed in the second commit: the probe read "no pending/claimed job row" as delivery evidence, but an SSE reconnect replays the durable input of a still-**running** turn (`registerWorker`), creating a fresh pending row for the same messageId — which made the running turn look undelivered and would have let a recycle SIGTERM an active worker. The probe now consults the positive delivery receipt instead (a **completed** `thread_message` row, retained 30 days), which is both simpler and correct for replay rows.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: targeted `bun test` on all 7 touched suites — 127 pass, 0 fail (includes the DB-backed resolver, enqueue, and liveness-probe suites; run locally against Postgres — the review-fix sandbox could not bind loopback ports, so its DB-suite pass is mine, not the fixer's)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] Full `make test-integration` sweep not run in this session; CI's integration job is the authoritative pass

### Red→green evidence
Red (dispatch gate disabled — mutation `if (this.dispatchRecycler)` → `if (false)` in `job-router.ts`):
```
 5 fail
 59 expect() calls
Ran 33 tests across 2 files.
```
Green (gate active, same suites):
```
 33 pass / 0 fail across worker-dispatch-recycle + worker-job-router
 127 pass / 0 fail across all touched suites
```

### Mutation evidence (each mutation applied to src, suite run, then reverted)
| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Disable the dispatch gate (`if (false)`) | 5 tests fail |
| M2 | Neutralize the live-turn probe (`if (false)`) | 1 test fails (mid-turn SIGTERM protection) |
| M3 | Fail open on recycle error (`throw` → `return`) | 1 test fails (fail-closed contract) |
| M4 | `LEASE_MIN_TTL_MS` 10min → 0 | 1 test fails (dying-token cache floor) |
| M5 | Drop resolved `appId` from token cache key | 1 test fails (App-repoint cache poisoning) |
| M6 | Revert probe to pending-row exclusion (pre-blocker-fix semantics) | 2 tests fail (reconnect-replay + foreign-receipt regressions) |
| M7 | Strip the replay queue-row predicate (pre-blocker-fix semantics) | 3 tests fail (pending/claimed/completed suppression regressions) |
| M8 | Revert rebuild-failure handling to plain rethrow (pre-blocker-fix semantics) | 1 test fails (terminalize-and-complete regression) |
| M9 | Re-add the internal error swallow in failTurnIfPending (pre-blocker-fix semantics) | 1 test fails (error-propagation pin) |

## Notes
- Supersedes #2234 (enqueue-side recycle; advisory-lock/hold-requeue approach). Closing it in favor of this PR.
- Net diff is +2,065/−129 across 19 files, of which ~57% is tests; there are no new tables, no deployment-name changes, and no new coordination primitives.
- Follow-up deliberately NOT planned: mid-turn lease refresh stays out of scope unless prod shows recycle churn or mid-turn 401s (tracked via post-rollout verification).
